## Pipeline Output & Data Specifications
*This section provides a detailed overview of the processed dataset generated by the pipeline.*

### 1. Dataset Summary
After running the preprocessing scripts, the Stanford COCA dataset is transformed into a standardized format ready for model training:
- **Total Samples:** Processed DICOM slices are converted into 2.5D stacks.
- **File Format:** High-performance `.npy` (NumPy) files for fast I/O during training.
- **Storage Path:** All outputs are structured within the `data/processed/` directory.

### 2. Technical Feature Specifications
Each output file follows a strict medical imaging standard:
| Feature | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Spatial Stacking** | **2.5D Technique** (3 consecutive slices: Prev, Current, Next) |
| **Input Shape** | `(3, 512, 512)` per tensor |
| **Pixel Intensity** | Standardized **Hounsfield Units (HU)** |
| **Windowing** | **Soft Tissue/Bone Contrast** (Window Level: 200, Window Width: 600) |
| **Clipping Range** | `[-100, 500] HU` (optimized for calcification visibility) |

### 3. Directory Layout (Output)
When the pipeline finishes, the `data/` folder will be populated as follows:
- `data/processed_npy/images/`: Contains the `.npy` files for the CT scans.
- `data/processed_npy/masks/`: Contains the corresponding binary ground-truth labels.

>  **Note for Reviewers:** To maintain repository speed, the actual `.npy` files are stored externally. You can verify the output quality by downloading the sample batch here: [**Google Drive Link**](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18Ka7Q3hTVjM2Zf0BZsQCM8fnXsPz982x?usp=sharing)
